Subject: Re: Capacity expansion during renewal - quick sync

Daniel — thanks for the CSV and for surfacing the p95 behavior. We dug through the runs and correlated spike windows with cold KV cache warmups + a couple of concurrent long-context samples (40k tokens). A quick summary of our findings: 

- Steady-state throughput at 60 req/s for model-xl on the reserved pool is achievable at queue depths we observed (we tested at 60–75 req/s for 30m).
- p95 spikes align with first-request cache misses and concurrent 40k-token threads; average p95 with cache warm (post-30s steady state) sits ~230–320ms.
- Without a burst pool, during noisy neighbor events we see short (1–3 min) tail latency bumps to ~800–950ms; with burst configured (2x transient headroom) those are absorbed.

I've attached our bakeshop report export and a Grafana snapshot. Recommendation: reserve the pool sized for 60 req/s steady, keep a small 2x burst buffer for the first 90 days, and enable prefix KV caching on your longest routes.

Next steps I propose:
1) Brightlane signs the amendment to add 6x A100 reserved slots (amendment attached).
2) We run a final 2-hour soak on November 10th with your production traffic replay.
3) Post-soak signoff call and we flip routing to Reserved+Burst.

I'll loop in Monica from CS to own the cutover runbook. Marissa and Karthik — please confirm SLA wording for the 60 req/s floor + burst policy.

Best,
Rishi
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Priya — good question. Short answer: burst is usage-based and only billed for the additional capacity consumed during bursts. We'll add a 'burst burn' meter on the daily invoice line for transparency and cap alerts (we can also set a hard cap if you need strict budget control). 

SLA language: proposed clause below (we're fine to make edits in redline):
"Redwood will maintain a steady throughput floor of 60 requests per second for the specified model variant on the Reserved Pool. Transient headroom (burst) of up to 2x may be available; burst consumption is billed on actual usage at the rate in Schedule B. Redwood will provide daily burst usage reporting for the first 90 days following expansion and will notify the customer if projected monthly burst spend exceeds 20% of the committed monthly spend."

Karthik — can you confirm monitoring hooks and a 30/7/1 observation cadence (30-minute aggregates, 7-day rolling alerts, daily ops check-ins for week 1)? Monica — please prepare the cutover runbook with rollback steps and the post-cutover verification checklist.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success

All — confirming monitoring/ops plan. TL;DR:
- We will enable per-route tracing + token-level latency buckets for the reserved pool. Dashboard will be pre-populated; snapshot included in earlier message.
- Alerting: p95 > 700ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows OR sustained queue depth > 250 triggers automated scale and ops pager.
- Post-cutover verification: run the 2-hour replay, validate p50/p95 and KV hit ratio, and run a synthetic 5k-request sample at the cutover marker.

I've scheduled the cutover window: Nov 11 02:00–04:00 UTC (to match your replay). Monica will own the rollback test and post-cutover verification; Rishi will own customer comms.

Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround on the signed amendment. We'll proceed with provisioning and keep you posted.

-Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
